**Phase 2 (post-training) contributes the larger gain.** It improves offline ranking metrics (MRR) by roughly **35–50%** compared with a freshly trained Phase-1 model. This is measured on the Phase-1 training cutoff date, when the Phase-1 model is at its freshest (p. 7, Section 5.3 and Table 1).

That gain grows over time. Two weeks later, the improvement rises to roughly **80%**. The authors attribute this to two things: the strength of task-specific adaptation, and the Phase-1 backbone going stale because it is updated less often (p. 7).

For comparison, using the Phase-1 foundation LLM as the base model improves offline ranking metrics by about **10–20%**. That figure is measured against an off-the-shelf (OSS) LLM backbone (p. 7, Section 5.3 and Table 1).

The two figures use different baselines. Phase 1 is compared with an OSS model, and Phase 2 is compared with a fresh Phase-1 model. Still, these are the figures the paper itself reports for each phase's contribution (p. 7).
